content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Design a geometric model consisting of two square plates, each with an edge length of 140mm and a thickness of 10mm. Position these plates so that they intersect at a 90-degree angle, creating an L-shape configuration. On one of these plates, incorporate a square cutout measuring 45x45mm. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (only describing what the future function call will do)

1. Establish the global coordinate system  
   • Origin (0, 0, 0).  
   • X-axis to the right, Y-axis to the back, Z-axis upward.

2. Add the first plate – the horizontal one  
   • Geometry: rectangular block.  
   • Size: 140 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z).  
   • Base-point: (0, 0, 0).  
   • subtraction flag: False (it creates the initial solid).

3. Add the second plate – the vertical one that intersects the first at 90°  
   • Geometry: rectangular block.  
   • Size: 10 mm (X – this is its thickness) × 140 mm (Y) × 140 mm (Z).  
   • Base-point: (0, 0, 0).  
   • Because its X-thickness (10 mm) lies exactly where the first plate begins, the two solids share the volume 0-10 mm in X and 0-10 mm in Z, creating the required L-shape intersection.  
   • subtraction flag: False (this is material to be kept).

4. Create the square cut-out through the horizontal plate  
   • Geometry: rectangular block that will be subtracted.  
   • Size: 45 mm (X) × 45 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z) – the full thickness of the horizontal plate.  
   • Base-point: centred in the horizontal plate but clear of the vertical one:  
     – X₀ = (140 – 45)/2 = 47.5 mm  
     – Y₀ = (140 – 45)/2 = 47.5 mm  
     – Z₀ = 0 mm  
   • subtraction flag: True (removes this volume, giving the 45 × 45 mm opening).

5. Combine all three solids in a single block() call by passing array values for every parameter:  
   • x_size  = [140, 10, 45]  
   • y_size  = [140, 140, 45]  
   • z_size  = [10, 140, 10]  
   • x       = [0, 0, 47.5]  
   • y       = [0, 0, 47.5]  
   • z       = [0, 0, 0]  
   • subtraction = [False, False, True]

6. After the block() call, issue finished(allFunctionsCalled=True) to signal completion.

When you are ready for me to output the actual function calls exactly as specified, just let me know.
